message.content:
**Norfolk Southern (CIK 702165) — railway operating ratio improved sharply in FY2024.**

**Reported (GAAP) results, fiscal year ended 2024-12-31 vs. 2023-12-31** (2024 Form 10-K, accession 0000702165-25-000008, filed 2025-02-10):

| Metric | 2024 | 2023 | 2022 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Railway operating revenues | $12,123M | $12,156M | $12,745M |
| Railway operating expenses | $8,052M | $9,305M | $7,936M |
| Income from railway operations | $4,071M | $2,851M | $4,809M |
| Railway operating ratio | **66.4%** | **76.5%** | 62.3% |

- The railway operating ratio (railway operating expenses ÷ railway operating revenues) **improved by 10.1 percentage points**, from 76.5% in 2023 to 66.4% in 2024 — i.e., operating expenses consumed a materially smaller share of revenue. My own check of the disclosed components gives 8,052/12,123 = 66.4% and 9,305/12,156 = 76.5%, consistent with the reported ratios (derived, not a separately disclosed field).
- Drivers per the filing: expenses fell 13% (including lower net Eastern Ohio Incident costs and $433M of gains on railway line sales), while revenues were roughly flat (lower fuel surcharge revenue, adverse traffic mix and lower pricing nearly offset by 5% higher volumes). Income from railway operations rose 43%.
- **Adjusted (non-GAAP) view:** excluding the Incident and 2024 items, the adjusted operating ratio was **65.8% in 2024 vs. 67.4% in 2023** (a 1.6 pp improvement), so part of the reported improvement is non-recurring. The 2023 reported ratio was inflated by $1.1B of net Incident costs (adjusted 2023: 67.4%).
- Longer trend (5-year statistics table): 2024 66.4%, 2023 76.5%, 2022 62.3%, 2021 60.1%, 2020 69.3% — so 2024 improved year-over-year but remained worse than 2021–2022.

**Sources:** 2024 10-K text chunks 702165/nsc-20241231:38400, :113600, :115200, :116800, :120000, :121600; structured facts: RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax FY2024 $12,123M (fact id 859736) and CostsAndExpenses FY2024 $8,052M (fact id 847174).

**Limitations:** The database's structured facts do not include a dedicated "operating ratio" tag or a FY2023 revenue/expense pair in the same series, so the ratio comparison relies on the 10-K's disclosed ratios and the FY2024 XBRL facts; the FY2023 figures ($12,156M revenue, $9,305M expenses) come from the 10-K text tables. The question did not specify a period, so I used the latest annual report available (FY2024).
